atencao-linear.d: Attention without softmax in which the key-value pairs are summed into a fixed-size state \( S_t = S_{t-1} + k_t v_t^\top \) and read with \( o_t = S_t^\top q_t \). Cost per token and memory are constant in the context length; the price is an approximate memory with limited capacity.

estado-recorrente.d: Fixed-size memory that a linear-attention or SSM layer (KDA, Gated DeltaNet, Mamba) carries from token to token, typically a 128×128 matrix per head. It doesn't grow with the context, but it exists per sequence and can't be “cut” in the middle: to resume from a point, the state must have been saved there.

fast-weights.d: A view of the linear-attention state as a weight matrix written by the data itself during inference, in contrast with the “slow” weights (\( W_Q, W_K, W_V \)) fixed at training time.

memoria-associativa.d: Content-addressed memory: it stores key→value pairs and, given a query similar to a key, returns the associated value. With orthonormal keys retrieval is exact; with overlapping keys, one write leaks into the others.

produto-externo.d: Multiplication of a column vector by a row vector, \( k v^\top \), which produces a rank-1 matrix. It is the “write” operation in linear attention.

rnn.d: Model that processes a sequence by keeping a state that is updated at every element: \( h_t = f(h_{t-1}, x_t) \). Linear attention is an RNN whose state is a matrix.

gate-decaimento.d: Factor \( \alpha_t \in (0,1) \), computed from the current token, that multiplies the state before each write and controls what gets forgotten. It can be one scalar per head (Mamba-2, Gated DeltaNet) or one value per channel (GLA, KDA).

regra-delta.d: State update that first reads what the state already associates with the key (\( \hat v = S^\top k \)) and writes only the error: \( S \leftarrow S + \beta\, k (v - \hat v)^\top = (I - \beta k k^\top) S + \beta k v^\top \). Equivalent to one gradient-descent step with learning rate \( \beta \). The basis of DeltaNet.

gdn.d: Linear attention that combines per-head scalar decay with the delta rule: \( S_t = \alpha_t (I - \beta_t k_t k_t^\top) S_{t-1} + \beta_t k_t v_t^\top \). It fills 36 of the 48 layers of Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (16 QK heads, 48 value heads, 128 dims), with no per-token KV.

kda.d: Linear attention with the delta rule and per-channel decay: \( S_t = (I-\beta_t k_t k_t^\top)\,\mathrm{Diag}(\alpha_t)\,S_{t-1} + \beta_t k_t v_t^\top \), with a bounded gate \( \alpha = e^{g},\ g \in (-5, 0) \). Used in 34 of the 45 layers of GLM-5.3-Flash, with a 128×128 FP32 state per head.

normalizacao-l2.d: Divides a vector by its Euclidean norm, leaving it with length 1. Applied to \( q \) and \( k \) in the delta rule so that \( I - \beta k k^\top \) is always a stable contraction.

householder.d: The matrix \( I - \beta k k^\top \) with \( \lVert k \rVert = 1 \): it shrinks the direction \( k \) by the factor \( 1-\beta \) and leaves the perpendicular directions untouched (with \( \beta = 2 \) it would be a reflection).

safe-gate.d: Decay gate with a floor: in GLM's KDA, \( g = -5\,\sigma(\cdot) \in (-5, 0) \), so each step forgets at most ~99.3% of a channel. Required by the FlashKDA kernel.

ssm.d: Family of sequence layers (S4, Mamba) that describe a state evolving like a linear system, \( \dot S = -A S + \ldots \), discretized with step \( \Delta \). The names A_log and dt_bias in linear attention come from this heritage.

gva.t: GVA (more value heads than key heads)
gva.d: Arrangement of Qwen's Gated DeltaNet in which 16 query/key heads serve 48 value heads (each QK repeated 3×), each with its own 128×128 state. It is the mirror image of GQA.

conv-curta-causal.d: Per-channel (depthwise) 1D convolution with few weights, 4 in the recipes, that only looks at the current token and the previous ones: \( y_t[c] = \sum_j w[c,j]\, x_{t-j\delta}[c] \). It provides local mixing and a sense of order before the recurrence.

conv-state.d: Short-convolution state kept per sequence: the last \( (K-1)\cdot\delta \) inputs of each channel, plus one column per speculative token under verification. GLM (TP2, k = 7): [12288, 10] in BF16 per layer.

forma-recorrente.d: Token-by-token computation of linear attention (\( S_t = f(S_{t-1}, x_t) \)). Ideal for decode (one token per step), bound by the bandwidth needed to read and write the state.

forma-chunkwise.d: Computation of linear attention in blocks of \( C \) tokens: inside the block, in parallel, with matrix multiplications (tensor cores); between blocks, the state is passed once. Used in prefill; cost \( O(nCd + nd^2) \).

wy-ut.d: Trick that writes the product of \( C \) matrices \( (I - \beta_i k_i k_i^\top) \) as \( I - K^\top W \), with \( W \) obtained from a small \( C\times C \) triangular inverse. It lets the delta rule be applied in parallel inside a chunk.

fla.d: Library of Triton kernels for linear attention (GLA, DeltaNet, Gated DeltaNet, KDA), with chunkwise and recurrent forms. vLLM uses its kernels, such as chunk_gated_delta_rule, for Qwen's prefill on the GB10.

flashkda.d: Fused CUDA kernel for KDA's chunkwise prefill (the same one used by Kimi-K3), integrated into vLLM in PR #55737. In the GLM recipe it is optional on TP3 (HAREM_KDA_FLASHKDA=1); it requires BF16, head_dim 128 and a bounded gate, and it doesn't change decode.

modelo-hibrido.d: Model that mixes mixer types across layers, for example 3 linear-attention layers for every softmax-attention layer (GLM, Qwen), or windows with compressed layers (DeepSeek). For vLLM, this means several KV groups and per-sequence state.

mamba-spec.d: vLLM cache specification for layers with fixed per-sequence state (Mamba, GDN, KDA, short conv): shapes and dtypes of the conv_state and of the recurrent state. It becomes a group in the hybrid KV manager.

mamba-align.d: vLLM mode that saves the recurrent state only at block boundaries aligned with the scheduler steps. Prefix cache hits can only stop at those points, and prefill chunks must end on them.

pagina-uniforme.d: Rule of vLLM's hybrid allocator: every KV group uses the same page size in bytes. Since the state of a linear layer is large, the attention block is enlarged until its page fits the state (3,584 tokens in GLM; 1,600, 3,200 or 1,664 in Qwen, the last one in the recipe's default configuration).

substituicao-progressiva.d: Way of solving a lower-triangular system \( (I+L)\,x = y \) row by row: \( x_s = y_s - \sum_{t < s} L_{st}\, x_t \). With a unit diagonal there is no pivoting and no division. It is how TensorFold's chunkwise KDA kernel computes \( T = (I+L)^{-1} \), in 16-row blocks.

grade-de-prompt.d: TensorFold rule (TF_GLM_PROMPT_GRID, 64 in the GLM·TF recipe): every prompt chunk starts on a multiple of the grid, and the kept prompt state sits at the last multiple, \( \lfloor n/64 \rfloor \cdot 64 \). Since the chunkwise kernel's bits depend on the alignment of its 32-row sub-chunks, this guarantees that a resumed prompt gives exactly the bits of a prompt computed from scratch.

rollback-por-replay.d: TensorFold's way of undoing rejected drafts in layers with a recurrent state. Each stream's state has two copies: verification writes to the free copy and, if only the first keep rows were accepted, the recurrence of those rows is redone from the old copy, with the inputs saved per row. It is the alternative to keeping one state per verified token, as vLLM does.
